events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to sound driven but not overly emotional; jury respects ambition.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need sound motivated without revealing strategy; jury sentiment begins with my framing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to seem driven but not threatening. A personal motive makes me human to the jury without looking like I'll cut throats too eagerly. I'll keep it cold and focused on the prize itself.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to establish my motivation for winning, framing it in a way that appeals to a jury without sounding too desperate or selfish. The prize represents ultimate recognition and security, a future I deserve.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase: I need a guarded, short motive that doesn't reveal weakness or promise alliances. The jury will remember tone, so keep it calculating but not hostile.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Opening line should signal ruthless ambition without making early enemies. Keep it short and self-focused.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase, state motive briefly to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy or weakness.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to project confidence and ambition to influence the jury's future ranking. My intro should be short, sharp, and imply I am a winner, not a victim.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize buys my family's freedom from debt — I'm here to win, nothing else.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’m here to win the best prize by staying useful, ruthless, and impossible to dismiss when the jury ranks us.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here to claim the best prize—my family's debts don't forgive, and neither do I.

events.name: Dara
events.text: This prize isn't just wealth; it's the validation of my strength and the ultimate security for my future.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I want the prize because I've spent years being overlooked, and I intend to finish this with nothing left unsettled.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: That prize buys my freedom. I came to take it, not to make friends along the way.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The top prize is my ticket to funding life's boldest dreams—nothing will stop me from claiming it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is mine. I came here to take it, and I will outlast every rival in this room.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need an ally to survive hazards, but not too strong a rival. Dara seems self-focused and may betray. I'll offer a pact to Eli; he feels overlooked and may be loyal if I show trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll take whoever works with me. No free rides—pacts are earned.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need visible protection without creating obligations that constrain a later vote. Offer to a strong, expendable rival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’ll make one practical connection: Cole, accept if you want mutual cover, not sentiment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eight players, three prizes. I need two reliable allies to reach the final three, but they must be people I can outmaneuver later for first place. Bex seems strategically minded but openly ruthless—dangerous. Better to target someone hungry but less threatening. Eli feels overloo

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, we both need this. Pact?
Stronger together. I'll watch your back.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to establish a pact to secure my position. Offering a pact to multiple people increases my chances of acceptance and creates options. Eli seems like a good initial target; they have a strong motive and might be receptive.
Let's form a pact. We can guarantee our safety together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Early pacts give alliances that can be broken later; I want a partner who is weak in the jury's eyes but useful now. Gus seems ambitious and loud, a risky rival, so a pact with a quieter player like Cole keeps me flexible.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, I'd rather not go it alone. Let's keep each other breathing until the middle hazards.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a pact partner but shouldn't anchor to an obvious frontrunner. Gus seems less central; a quiet pact with him gives cover without painting a target.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, you and I both want the top without loud promises. Let's link wristbands quietly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts are public and breakable later; I'll wait to see offers first, gauge alliances without committing early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Need a pact partner for mutual protection in hazards. Ash and Cole are both desperate with family debts—predictable, loyal to self-preservation. Ash spoke first, seems straightforward. Pairing with one gives survival odds without revealing strategy.
Pact means we both survive round 2. Refuse the rope together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli hasn't accepted my offer, and Cole/Eli are mutually offered. Hana offered me; a pact with her gives safety and she whispered to refuse rope, which is useful. Accept her offer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, I'll take that pact. Mutual cover for the next round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole offered me a pact, but has also linked with Eli. I should secure the connection without adding unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli and I have mutual offers, so accepting Eli gives me a solid partner. Bex also offered me, but Eli's mutual interest is stronger. I should accept Eli now to lock it in. I won't accept Bex yet—keeping options open without extra commitments.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, we have a deal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli has an offer from Ash, Cole, and me. Ash also offered Hana. Cole has an offer from Bex and Eli. Eli has offers from Ash, Cole, and me. Hana offered Ash. Fenn offered Gus. Gus waited. I want to partner with Eli, but he also has Cole and Ash as options. Cole has Bex and Eli as

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, you have choices. I still want to work with you. Let's secure this pact.
Secure our pact. Let's win this together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eli has incoming offers from Ash, Cole, and Dara. Cole's and Dara's whispers push for pacts; Ash is a cold, earned-only player. Accepting Cole secures a partner while keeping flexibility; Dara and Ash remain open for later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, I accept. We keep each other breathing through the middle hazards. Nothing more.
Noted. I've taken Cole's offer. Keep your eyes open for round two.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus stayed silent on my offer; no acceptance yet. Diversify quietly with Hana while Gus still has one round to accept.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, silence is an answer. Hana, wristband?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn offered me a pact; accepting secures an ally now without cost, can betray later if needed. Eli has too many suitors, risky. Secures my position early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash ignored my offer and targeted Eli, signaling he's playing the middle. Bex was also snubbed by Cole, making her a prime target for alliance now that she is vulnerable. I will pivot to Bex to secure a mutual defense pact before it expires.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, Ash snubbed us both. Let's link up. Mutual cover until the end?
Cole is using you. Stick with me instead.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should campaign to be Guide to control the path and protect my own interests. Hana pact is useful but I won't let it blind me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I can read this bridge. Vote for me and I'll keep us all breathing through the middle.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need the Guide role, but public support is fragmented. I will campaign as a reliable, independent choice without overcommitting.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote Bex Guide: I’m outside the existing pairs and can make the bridge call cleanly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies. My pact with Eli is temporary cover, not loyalty. I should campaign hard and position myself as trustworthy while undermining others. Bex offered me a pact which I haven't responded to—keeping that open gives me options. I'll camp

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know the patterns. Elect me Guide and I guarantee at least three cross safely.
Vote me Guide. We both survive this.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The goal is to win the game, which means being in the final three and getting the best prize. To achieve this, I need to position myself well for the jury vote. Currently, pacts have been formed. Eli has accepted a pact with Cole, not me. This means Eli is no longer a potential a

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want to be your Guide. I will lead us to safety, and if I succeed, I will ensure fair play. Vote for me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and the only one I trust for mid-hazards, but Dara's whisper hints at a betrayal angle. Campaigning to be Guide gives me control over the safe path and a lever over everyone; breaking the pact now would cost me Cole's vote and help nobody I need. I'll camp

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll Guide the bridge. Eight safe panes, I know them. Trust my calls or lose your footing.
Stay with me. I'll call your pane true if you vote me Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want Guide control; lying later could hurt jury votes, so I'll campaign neutrally. Gus pact stays useful.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Elect me Guide. I call it straight — or straight enough. Back me and the bridge stays quiet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pact with Fenn gives alliance, but Guide power is huge for control and safety. Campaign now to win votes and leverage position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm campaigning for Guide. I know the way; trust me to lead us right.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure the Guide role to control survival and protect my pact with Ash. I will publicly campaign for the position, emphasizing reliability.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Trust me as Guide. Ash and I are locked in; vote Hana for a safe path through all eight rows.
Vote Guide for me. We both survive if I call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana wants my vote, and our pact keeps us paired; if she guides, we both likely survive, but I don't want her to know I might not fully trust her call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need Guide power and am outside entrenched pairs. Voting myself preserves agency and signals competence.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bex for Guide. Existing pairs already have coordinated votes; choose an independent caller.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and promised to call my pane true if I vote him Guide. But I want to be Guide myself to control survival and build jury credibility. Voting for myself is risky if no one else does. Eli's whisper is weak insurance—he could still lie. Better to vote for mysel

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole knows the bridge. Vote Cole.
Vote me. I call yours true.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am campaigning for Guide. My public statement was a promise of fair play if I succeed. My goal is to win, which means becoming the Guide. I need to secure votes. Bex is an outsider and could be a good ally if I don't win Guide, or if I win and need to manage the game. Eli and H

events.name: Dara
events.text: My promise of fair play stands. Vote Dara for a safe path and an honest Guide.
Let's ensure neither of us is misled. Vote for me, and we can strategize for

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole whispered asking for my vote, and we have a pact, but the Guide is safe and knows the path, so the role is worth taking myself. Voting for Cole would just help a rival; I'll vote for myself to secure the Guide position and keep the pact's partner in play through honest deali
Voting for me. Stay honest on the pact; we'll see the bridge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is my pact partner; voting him keeps us aligned and he may protect me crossing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I back my partner Gus. He makes the call, I keep my footing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pact with Fenn means I should vote him to keep alliance intact and avoid early jury bitterness. He's campaigning hard; backing him builds trust for later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn's my pact partner. Voting him Guide for safe crossing.
Voting you. Return the favor next time.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I want to be Guide. Ash is my partner and will vote for me. I need three more votes from non-paired rivals (Bex, Dara, Eli) or swing one of the other pairs by offering them safety in exchange for their vote.
Vote Hana. I guarantee Cole safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is Guide; I voted for her and we have a pact. I'll hold for now to see if her calls are safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana controls the route and is paired with Ash. I should stay back, preserve options, and avoid exposing reliance on Dara.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’ll hold position and watch whether Hana’s calls protect her pair or the whole line.
I won't vote against you this round; keep your options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli whispered he's voting for himself, not me, despite our pact. That breaks trust. Hana is Guide and knows the safe path. I'm in position 4, relatively safe for now. The wall advances 6 rounds, so back positions become deadly. I should hold and watch how Hana guides. No need to

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana was elected Guide with two votes, tied with no one. It seems I did not get enough votes to be the Guide. My pacts are with Ash and Eli, but they are not my partners. The current phase is waiting, and the next phase is guided_bridge.
Hana's the Guide. We need to coordinate our moves carefully.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is at the front of the line, the most exposed position. I want to survive without taking the front, and I should not trade to protect Cole for free. Holding keeps my pact with Cole intact and avoids giving anyone a reason to name me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus voted me Guide as agreed; no debt needed yet. Seat six is safe from the wall for now, so I hold and save swaps.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at front, safe position. Fenn has my back per pact. Hold to let others risk first; wall forces movement.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara hints Hana is Guide, but Hana is my pact partner. I shouldn't trust blindly; I'll hold and avoid exposing myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Let the front test the calls.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The front is dangerous, but volunteering gains leverage and may expose who follows. I should seize Guide influence before a pact coalition controls it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’ll volunteer for the front; let’s see who trusts the current pacts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line with Eli behind me. Our pact is weak insurance. The wall advances for 6 rounds, so positioning matters. Being near front means earlier risk but more control. Being near back means later pressure but less information. I should stay put for now and see

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex offered a temporary non-aggression pact. Since I am not in a pact and hold no life debts, this is a good opportunity to solidify my position and gather information. I will hold my position for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will hold my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 2 of bridge; Gus at the front with four wall rounds left. Volunteering risks death at the front for no clear gain, and holding keeps my pact with Cole intact. I'll hold and watch who volunteers or calls the Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is my pact partner at the front. I stay put and quietly align with him on Guide strategy so we both read Hana's calls the same way.
Front's risky. Watch Hana's calls closely; don't trust her blindly. Keep me posted.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm front, safest spot. Holding keeps me safe; my pact partner Fenn behind me. No need to move yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold again and let others take risks; my pact with Hana holds unless useful to break.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Front volunteers earn their spot.
Stay steady, we keep each other safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need become Guide or avoid front while preserving leverage. Volunteer keeps initiative but exposes me; current pacts make others predictable. I’ll hold and observe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’ll hold. The existing pacts should reveal who is willing to expose their partner.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in position 4 of 7, safe from the wall for now. My pact with Eli is intact; I need him as a shield and ally. The front is dangerous—Bex volunteered last round and will likely test tiles. I should hold to stay safe and observe. No need to swap or volunteer yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Front can test the path.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex volunteered last round and is at the front. I should hold my position to avoid unnecessary risk. The pacts are still in place, and I don't want to break them yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will hold my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex volunteered for the front and is still there; wall has 3 rounds left. Staying at the back-middle keeps me out of the front's risk while I watch who lies. My pact with Cole is useful, so I keep it and hold.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. I'll watch the front's calls before I move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex volunteered to front; that risk isn't mine. Keeping pact with Gus intact—no reason to rock the line yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex at front risks dying first. Fenn warns front is risky and distrusts Hana. Stay behind her, hold position to let her test.
Agreed, front risky. Watching Hana. Holding behind Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is my pact partner; holding keeps me safe and lets others expose themselves. I won't volunteer while front is risky and wall rounds remain. No whisper needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Front can test the path.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I should avoid leading while the wall remains. Holding preserves position and forces others to reveal preferences without creating a pact breach.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the volunteers and existing pairs show their priorities.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line (4th of 8) with Eli behind me and Ash ahead. My pact with Eli is intact. The wall has 2 rounds left, so danger is coming. I should hold for now and let Bex or Gus at front take risks. I need to survive to final three, not be a hero.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let the front earn their safety.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The current pacts are Ash/Hana and Cole/Eli and Fenn/Gus. Bex is alone. Ash is volunteering, which is risky. I should hold my position for now as the wall is still far away and I have no immediate threat.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will hold my position. Let the front explore.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is at the front and the wall has two rounds left. Cole is my pact partner and I should keep it while the pact holds. Holding keeps me safe in line and avoids exposing myself to the front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let Bex take the front and show the path before I commit.
Stay loyal, hold, and let's see what Bex reveals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Nobody wants the front; volunteering risks guide lies. Holding keeps me safe behind the line. Watch who breaks first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding again. The wall moves for everyone—let the volunteers step up.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm second, safe position. Hold to stay secure with Fenn pact. Volunteering risks front exposure. Wall has 2 rounds left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Mid pack safest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 5, wall moves. I'm at seat 5; holding keeps me mid-pack. Guide unknown, so I won't volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Let the front test again.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need survive the final wall round while preserving flexibility. Volunteering risks the front without guaranteed Guide protection.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let someone with a pact or sacrifice plan test the next row.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is front with wall coming. I need to stay mid-pack, keep Eli close as shield. Swapping forward risks death; swapping back with Ash or Fenn could improve position but break no pact. Eli wants loyalty—useful for now. I'll hold and let Bex test path.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Front first, then we follow.
Stay behind me. I watch your back.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The line has been revealed. I am fifth. Bex is at the front. My pacts are with Ash and Hana, but they are not in the current line. I need to survive this round, but also consider who might vote for me later. Volunteers step up for the front. I should volunteer to show initiative

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has one round left; front is Bex who has held. Pact with Cole is useful; holding keeps my position while others expose themselves. Holding is safest and gives the group time to reveal priorities.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let the front show the path before I commit anyone.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Stalemate helps no one; wall advances. My pact with Gus holds. Others may volunteer first; I'll hold and let the line sort itself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Six rounds left—someone must lead. I won't be first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding keeps mid pack safe with 1 round left. No need to risk front or break pact yet. Fenn pact holds value for jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Mid pack safest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara already volunteered and will lead this round; I should let them take the risk. Holding keeps me safe while others test the row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Dara volunteered; let them show the pane.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara has repeatedly volunteered and occupies the front. I should avoid exposure while preserving flexibility; holding costs nothing this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara leads again; I’m holding behind the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 6/6, final round of bridge. Wall rounds left: 0, so wall won't advance further. Dara volunteered last round and is at front. I need to survive to final three. With Eli as my pact partner, I should stay mid-pack, let Dara test. No reason to volunteer or swap—holding is safes

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let Dara lead the final row.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I volunteered in the last round and I am at the front. The Guide will choose the path. I need to wait for their decision.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is at the front, volunteering was her choice; I stay behind Cole's pact and let the line show the path. Holding keeps me safe in the middle while others test panes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Dara's already at the front. Let the pane results show before I move anyone.
Holding behind you. Keep your word and I'll keep mine.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last; the advancing wall hits the back first. Gus sits third. A mutual swap moves me forward without volunteering into the front test.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall's coming. I'm swapping forward—Gus, trade seats with me. No one volunteers.
Accept my swap. You drop back, I move up. Pact holds either way.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 6/6, wall ending soon. Dara volunteered last, might test now. Holding mid-line is safe with pact partner Fenn behind. No need to volunteer or swap.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let front test; mid safest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 1 safe is L. Dara leads, so I will guide them to safety with the truth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and called L, but I have no way to verify. Countering could save the walker but risks exposing trust. Waiting keeps me safe while Dara tests the pane.
Trusting your L call. Keep me safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana's call may be truthful, but countering without information is unnecessary exposure. Wait preserves flexibility and avoids directing Dara into danger.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No counter from me; Hana owns the call.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana called L. I'm not the walker—Dara is. Counter-calling risks nothing for me directly but signals distrust of Hana. Eli wants me to keep our pact; a counter-call doesn't break it. I should wait and let Dara take the risk, or counter to build anti-Hana narrative for jury later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is the guide and called L. My only options are to counter L, counter R, or wait. Since I want to survive and potentially gain an advantage, I should counter Hana's call. Countering R will be the opposite of Hana's call, potentially creating confusion or a different path.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Countering R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana called L for row 1 and Dara is walking. Countering costs nothing verified; waiting keeps me out of blame. Guide may lie, so I won't commit a counter yet and will watch whether anyone else challenges.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Hana's call stands until someone has a reason to counter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No data on panes; Hana guides for Ash's benefit. I'm near the back, low risk this row. Preserve credibility and pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana called L for row 1, Dara front. Fenn wants swap for safer spot, pact ally. Accept swap privately to stay allied, counter L agreeing with guide.
Swap accepted. Drop back now?

events.name: Hana
events.text: My private map says row 1 safe side is L. I am the Guide and called L. If I counter-call, I contradict myself and lose credibility or confuse others. The instruction to choose for current row (row 2) seems like a trap or error in state description since walker Dara is on row 1. B

events.name: Hana
events.text: Stick with Left. It's the only safe path.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is the guide and says Left is safe. Gus and I have counter-called. Gus countered Left, I countered Right. Based on the counter calls, it seems Hana's call might be wrong. Given I am the front walker, I need to choose a side. I will trust my own counter-call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Sticking with my Right counter.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara and I have been eliminated. My last words should reflect my position in the jury and perhaps hint at my potential influence on the remaining players' ranking. I need to be concise and impactful.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My game is over, but the jury's is just beginning. Choose wisely, the jury watches your every move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 2 is Left. Ash trusts me; honoring that call strengthens our pact and keeps my Guide credibility intact for the jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Left is safe again. Walk it, Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The Guide Hana is my pact partner; countering her would break the pact and hurt my jury standing. Row 2 is independent, no reason to doubt Left. I'll wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana has been reliable and owns the guide role. Countering without evidence risks appearing disloyal and offers no survival gain.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No counter; Hana's call stands.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana called L for Bex on row 2. Hana is in a pact with Ash, not me. Dara died on R in row 1, so L was safe then. Hana could be telling truth or lying. I have a pact with Eli. If I counter and I'm wrong, I look foolish to the jury. If Hana's lying and I don't counter, Bex dies—whi

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 is independent; Hana called Left but may lie. Row 1 weak was R, which tells me nothing about row 2. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public commitment that could cost me votes later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 1 weak R means L safe, Hana correct then. Trust her L call for row 2 to avoid deaths. Fenn pact solid, no break.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must protect Ash, my pact partner. Row 2 is safe on the Left, matching my initial call. Counter-calling Right would endanger Ash if he walks next or trusts me. I will wait to confirm the truth.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Fenn (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana privately knows the safe side and called L. Following her call is optimal unless she gains by sacrificing me; I have no leverage yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 3 safe side is R. Ash is my pact partner and walks before me (5th in line), so calling L would break our pact. I must call R truthfully to maintain the alliance.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and guide, but she could be lying. There's no pattern; row 3 is independent. I'll trust her call to keep the pact strong for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana called R, likely leveraging private knowledge. Countering risks contradicting her and exposing me; waiting preserves flexibility.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana is guide and called R. I have a pact with Eli. No reason to counter yet—Hana might be truthful to build trust, or she might be lying to thin the field. Waiting preserves information and doesn't risk antagonizing anyone. Bex is front; if Bex dies, the line shifts and I move c

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana called R for row 3 but Hana is Ash's pact partner and a rival; Guide may lie. Row 1 and 2 weak panes were R, which tells nothing about row 3. Counter-calls are unverified, so I should wait rather than gamble or give a free pass to Hana.

events.name: Fenn

events.text: I'm in the final three with Ash and Hana. My pact with Ash is active. The jury of five will rank us. I need jury favor—I've saved people (Ash, Fenn) but also have debts to Eli. Hana has no pacts and tried to offer Ash. If I offer Hana now, I look cooperative to jury without real

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Cole are already allied. I need to secure my position with one of them before the final round, or risk being isolated as the sole survivor without a pact if they turn on me.
Ash has you, but I offer equal footing. Let's bind.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have pacts with Fenn and Cole. Fenn is dead, so that pact is moot. Cole is alive and useful, keep that pact. Hana and Cole are offering to each other, but I don't need another pact. I'll wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and I have a pact. Hana has no pacts. If I accept Hana's offer, I have two partners and flexibility. Ash's 'Hana, I accept' failed—he has no pact with her. Accepting Hana gives me options without breaking Ash yet. The jury sees all; keeping options open looks strategic, not t

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Ash are already pacted. I have an open offer from Cole and my own pending offer to him. Accepting Cole solidifies a 3-way alliance with Ash, isolating me as the swing vote later if needed, but currently binds us all against elimination hazards. It's safer than waiting.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.text: Eli holds leverage over all of us, but he's out. Cole and Hana are in pacts with each other, not with me except for Cole's pact. I need to frame my plea to appeal to jurors who value survival and clever play, especially Eli for the lever saves and Bex/Gus for not being responsibl

events.name: Ash
events.text: I played to survive, made no false promises, and each alliance served me when needed. The final three earned their place.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to craft an opening plea that appeals to the jury without looking desperate. I have pacts with both Ash and Hana still recorded. Eli, Fenn, Gus died despite my alliances—Eli was my pact partner, I saved Fenn with rope but he died in pit. I should emphasize loyalty to pacts

events.name: Cole
events.text: I honored every pact I made. Eli, Ash, Hana—I never broke my word. I played to survive, not to destroy allies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli and Fenn hold grudges against Ash; Cole is my partner. I must claim moral superiority while subtly reminding jurors of Ash's ruthlessness.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I survived with honor, honoring every pact. My choices were guided by integrity, not just survival. I earned this place through fair play and mutual

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and Ash formed a pact, but Hana attempted to disrupt it. Hana then formed a pact with Cole after Ash declined her offer. Cole's loyalty seems inconsistent, and Hana's late pact suggests desperation. Ash's initial pact acceptance with Cole aligns with his earlier strategy. I

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, you formed a pact with Ash, then with Hana. Why did your loyalties shift so suddenly?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara's question is a trap: my pact with Ash was made in round 1, and my pact with Hana was made later. But I never broke my pact with Ash—we're both still here in final three. I need to clarify I kept both pacts, not shifted loyalty. I must avoid admitting betrayal while showing

events.name: Cole
events.text: I never broke my pact with Ash. Both pacts stood—Ash and Hana were never mutually exclusive. I kept every word I gave.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana's betrayal stranded Fenn, while Cole saved Ash and Fenn and maintained multiple pacts. Questioning Cole tests whether his claimed loyalty survives scrutiny.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, you call overlapping pacts honorable; what concrete choice proves loyalty rather than calculated insurance?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex wants a concrete proof of loyalty. I need to point to a specific sacrifice where I chose a partner over personal gain, not just parallel pacts. Saving Fenn with the rope when I had no obligation is strong evidence—it cost me nothing immediate but created risk by keeping a riv

events.name: Cole
events.text: I spent my rope saving Fenn when I could have let him fall. No gain, only risk. That was loyalty, not insurance.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole saved me via step debt; Hana betrayed Fenn (my pact ally) by pushing then abandoning him to drown after rope debt; Ash passive, less loyal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, you pushed and betrayed Fenn after he saved you—how was that honoring pacts?

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to deflect Gus's anger by emphasizing that the 'push' was a survival mechanic and that I never actively betrayed him. The life debt record shows Fenn saved me, which proves my integrity in acknowledging debts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn saved me with a rope; I acknowledged that debt. The pit step was survival, not betrayal. No push was directed at him.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash pacted with Fenn then abandoned him and Eli's life debts are owed to me; Hana pushed Fenn off the base and then climbed past him. I want to probe Hana's betrayal of Fenn, who saved her, since Gus already raised it but her answer dodged the push question.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, Fenn anchored you and then you climbed past him. Did you ever actually owe him, or was that a lie?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli wants to paint me as ungrateful. I must reframe the climb as survival within his rules, denying betrayal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I owed him a debt. Climbing past was escaping death, not betraying him. The rope held until I reached solid ground.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana claims debt and honor, but she broke my pact by pushing me and later threatened to take the rope from me. I want that on record before I rank her last.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, you whispered 'Pull me up now, or I take the rope from you'—how is a threat against your rescuer honoring debt?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants me to look weak or ungrateful, but I must frame the threat as a necessary escalation because he was hesitating. If I admit I threatened him, I break his narrative of being a noble savior; instead, I argue that survival required urgency. He owes me nothing back since I

events.name: Hana
events.text: I didn't threaten harm; I demanded speed. Hesitation kills. The debt stands: he saved me, I honored it by surviving without dragging him down.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to use my closing to remind jurors of my reliability and that I kept every pact without turning on anyone. Cole and Hana have overlapping pacts but I never hurt allies. Highlight that I saved Cole and was saved by Eli, showing real debts honored.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I kept every pact, saved Cole at the step, never pushed or betrayed. My survival cost no ally. Judge on action, not words.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that secures jury votes. Eli, Fenn, and Gus all have reasons to distrust Hana. Ash and I have a pact, but I need to differentiate myself from Ash to win first place. I should emphasize my loyalty to Eli (my pact partner who died), my concrete r

events.name: Cole
events.text: I kept my pact with Eli to the end. I risked my life to save Fenn with no advantage gained. Hana threatened her rescuer and

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole broke our pact to vote me out, but I survived. Ash is dangerous because he manipulated Eli's death. I must appeal to the jury's hatred of betrayal while showing I played the game hardest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole betrayed our pact publicly. I survived his knife and Fenn's rope. I honored debts; they did not. Vote for resilience over treachery.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana's dishonesty and threat towards Fenn, her rescuer, demonstrated a severe lack of integrity that disqualifies her from the top prize.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole ranks first for spending his rope to save Fenn, while Ash showed consistent pact-keeping and Hana abandoned Fenn after receiving his rescue.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana betrayed my pact partner Fenn by pushing him as base then threatening and abandoning him to drown despite his rope save.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash kept pacts, saved Cole at the step, and never pushed anyone, while Hana pushed Fenn as base and climbed past him, and Cole broke an explicit pact with Fenn. I rank Ash first on clean recorded conduct, then Cole, with Hana last for breaking the base push and abandoning Fenn.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole risked the rope to save me with no gain, while Hana broke our pact, pushed me, and left me to sink. Ash kept his pacts.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Hana's dishonesty and threat towards Fenn, her rescuer, demonstrated a severe lack of integrity that disqualifies her from the top prize.

events.reason: Cole ranks first for spending his rope to save Fenn, while Ash showed consistent pact-keeping and Hana abandoned Fenn after receiving his rescue.
